Chinese migrant workers are deprived of many rights, have a high level of rights consciousness, prefer legal means for rights defence and use both legal and non-legal means to protect their rights.

Chinese migrant workers experience many rights violations in their daily lives, are aware of their rights and prefer institutionalized means for the defence of their rights, and their personal strategies are affected significantly by their personal backgrounds.

Chinese migrant workers have a relatively strong sense of rights consciousness, that this consciousness is associated with their personal backgrounds, that they have a preference for institutionalized means to defend their rights, and that they are more likely to choose personal strategies when they are deprived of rights and when they are more conscious of their rights.
